title: SubZeroDev Plugin Result Envelope
description: Normative envelope schema. Every plugin writes exactly one instance of this to stdout in JSON mode; every host parses it. The $id is version-pathed so publishing 1.1 or 2.0 cannot overwrite a pinned reference.

schemaVersion.description: Envelope schema version, independent of the plugin's own version. A host refuses a higher major and accepts a higher minor.

command.description: The command ID that ran, matching a commands[].id in the manifest.

status.description: Duplicates what the exit code says, deliberately, so an adapter can branch on a word rather than memorize a table. The allOf below keeps the two from disagreeing.

summary.description: One human-readable sentence. Present even on success, so a host has something to show without opening data or an artifact.

finishedAt.description: Must be at or after startedAt. JSON Schema cannot express the comparison; conformance tests it.

data.description: A summary, not a payload, capped at 256 KiB serialized. Anything larger must be an artifact. The cap is not expressible here; conformance tests it. Emit {} rather than omitting.

warnings.description: Conditions worth reporting that did not degrade the result. Emit [] rather than omitting.

errors.description: Structured failure reporting. A failed or partial status must carry at least one entry — enforced by the status conditionals below, since an empty errors array leaves the host nothing to act on.

artifacts.description: Registration records for what was actually written this run, not the manifest's declaration of what may be. Emit [] rather than omitting.

metrics.description: Numeric counters a host can aggregate across runs — request counts, byte totals, durations in milliseconds. Values are numbers so aggregation needs no per-plugin knowledge. Emit {} rather than omitting.

exitCode.description: The process exit code, restated so the envelope stands alone. 1 is reserved and never assigned: it is what most runtimes return for an uncaught exception, and 'the plugin crashed' must stay distinguishable from 'the plugin reported a failure'.

plan.description: Present only on the read-only half of a plan-apply pair. Top-level rather than inside data so the approval gate is observable by a host that knows nothing about the plugin.

exitCode.description: A failure is 2, 3, 5, 6, or a plugin-specific code in 7-113. The four codes that carry their own status are excluded.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339, UTC, Z-suffixed. A local offset is refused: one representation keeps host-side comparison and ordering free of timezone handling. The pattern bounds each component, so 2026-99-99T99:99:99Z is rejected; the `:60` second is permitted because RFC 3339 allows a leap second. Month-specific day counts and leap years are calendar rules a regular expression cannot express — `format: date-time` covers them for validators that assert formats, and conformance covers the rest.

id.description: Matches the manifest id, e.g. subzerodev.github.

code.description: Stable machine-readable identifier, e.g. repository_statistics_unavailable. Policy keys on this, so it must not change with the message wording.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Must contain no secret: it reaches logs, execution history, and often a screen.

subject.description: What the diagnostic is about, by convention type:id — for example repository:12345. The identifier is a string even when the provider's is numeric.

retryable.description: The plugin knows most about the failure, so it advises the retry policy rather than leaving the host to guess from an exit code.

name.description: Matches a manifest artifacts[].name where one was declared. An undeclared artifact is retained and flagged, not discarded.

path.description: Relative to the output directory, normalized, and confined to it. Both separators are refused as a leading character and as traversal, because the contract supports Windows plugins: this rejects /etc/passwd, \\server\share, C:\secret, ../etc, and a\..\b alike. A host must still canonicalize the resolved path and verify containment — a pattern cannot see where a symlink points.

bytes.description: Size on disk. Lets a host decide whether to fetch before fetching.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex, unprefixed. This is what makes determinism checkable: an unchanged rerun produces the same digest.

planId.description: Opaque and random, never a hash of the content — a guessable plan ID is not a gate. The apply command accepts this and nothing else.

fingerprint.description: Digest of the target state the plan was computed against. The apply command refuses when the target no longer matches: applying a stale diff over someone's manual change is worse than refusing.

rendering.description: The diff a human reviews before approving. Required and non-empty: a plan token an operator can accept with nothing to look at is a rubber stamp, not a gate.
